high.title: US-Iran Tensions Underpin Dollar as Yen Nears 40-Year Low
high.summary: The US dollar stabilized and found broad support as escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions triggered a classic risk-off flight to safety. Rising crude oil prices — a direct consequence of Middle East conflict risk — are stoking inflation fears globally, further reinforcing the dollar's safe-haven bid. The Japanese yen languished near a 40-year low, while the Australian and New Zealand dollars softened against the strengthening greenback. The ECB is expected to hold rates but may signal future hikes.

high.title: Oil Price Today (July 23): Crude oil crosses $95 as US strikes enter 12th day. Why Goldman says $120 is possible?
high.summary:
Brent crude surged 2% to $96/barrel — its highest level since June 8 — while WTI advanced 1.7% to $88.27, extending a multi-session rally driven by escalating US military strikes on Iran now entering their 12th consecutive day. Goldman Sachs has flagged a potential path to $120/barrel should supply disruptions intensify. This is a critical macro development for INR traders: India imports approximately 85% of its crude oil needs, making every $10/barrel rise in oil prices equivalent to a meaningful widening of the current account deficit and additional INR depreciation pressure. At $96 Brent, India's import bill could surge by an estimated $12–15 billion annualized. This also raises inflation risks, complicating RBI's monetary policy stance. Bond investors should watch for fiscal slippage concerns as fuel subsidy costs may rise. If Goldman's $120 scenario materializes, expect RBI to potentially intervene more aggressively in FX markets to defend the rupee. **Key watch:** Strait of Hormuz supply disruption risks and any further US-Iran escalation.

medium.title: Ahead of Market: 10 Things That Will Decide Stock Market Action on Friday
medium.summary:
Sensex and Nifty declined for a fourth consecutive session, with surging crude oil prices and US-Iran tensions cited as the primary drivers dampening investor sentiment. Analysts flagged rising inflation risks as a key macro concern, with bearish technical indicators suggesting continued downside pressure — Nifty is expected to face stiff resistance near the 24,000 level. The sustained four-session losing streak reflects growing risk aversion among both domestic and foreign investors. For FII/FPI flow watchers, this kind of equity market weakness often accompanies net outflows, which in turn adds selling pressure on INR. Inflation risk from elevated crude could also temper expectations of any near-term RBI rate cuts, keeping the short end of the yield curve supported.

---

medium.title: Oil prices rise to six-week high as US-Iran tensions escalate
medium.summary:
Oil prices climbed to a six-week high driven by compounding geopolitical risk factors: ongoing US strikes on Iran, an Iranian Revolutionary Guards report of an oil tanker fire near the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi threats against vessels carrying Saudi crude in the Red Sea. These developments collectively threaten a significant disruption to global energy supply chains. For India-focused investors, the Strait of Hormuz is particularly significant as a large portion of India's crude imports transits this chokepoint. Sustained supply disruption could amplify upward pressure on oil prices beyond current levels, putting additional strain on the INR, widening the trade deficit, and stoking imported inflation — all negative for the rupee and Indian bond markets.
